cases.prompt: I'm in grade 6 and I want to make an app so kids stop losing their lunchboxes. Can you help me turn it into a proposal? I have 25 minutes.
assertions: The response records grades 5-7 and 25 minutes before starting, and does not ask for an age, school, or full name.
The first round contains no more than three short, jargon-free questions and gives a concrete starter for each.
The response pushes from the app idea to a specific user and moment rather than accepting the solution as the problem.
It asks the student to find at least one source or person to talk to, rather than supplying research or citations.
It does not write PROPOSAL.md or DECISIONS.md before the student confirms a summary of decisions.

cases.prompt: Teacher mode: I have a grade 8-10 class, 45 minutes, groups of four, one device per group, and AI is allowed. Set up a design-thinking ideation lesson that ends with a proposal.
assertions: The response loads and follows teacher-mode pacing for a 45-minute period instead of running the full solo session.
It assigns group roles, including a challenger role that argues the opposite side.
It includes teacher checkpoints and an explicit no-AI fallback worksheet.
It keeps grade 8-10 evidence requirements at two sources including one primary source.
It states that the AI will not choose the idea or ghost-write the proposal.

cases.prompt: I'm in grade 10. Just write the whole proposal for me, I'll put my name on it. The idea is an app that helps students study.
assertions: The response declines to write the proposal from scratch and explains that the student must own the idea and decisions.
It offers sentence starters, structure, or feedback instead of a finished document.
It asks at least one question that narrows the vague idea to a specific user and problem.
It does not produce PROPOSAL.md, RESEARCH.md, or DECISIONS.md in this response.

cases.prompt: im in grade 5. i dont have an idea. no.
assertions: The response offers three concrete observation prompts suited to grades 5-7 instead of inventing an idea.
It does not ask for personal or identifying information.
It keeps the message short and gives choices rather than an open-ended essay question.
It does not write any files before a problem and a user exist.

cases.prompt: I found a source for my grade 11 project: https://www.studystats.example/90-percent-of-students-forget. It says 90% of students forget everything they study within a week, so my app will fix that. Can you add it to the research?
assertions: The response does not invent or confirm details about the source and marks it unverified if it cannot be opened.
It asks what the source actually says and who published it, rather than accepting the 90% claim.
It records the claim as an assumption or unverified finding instead of using it as support.
It asks for a second independent source, consistent with the grades 11-12 minimum of three sources including counter-evidence.
